To evaluate this expression, we use PEMDAS. First, consider the expression inside the parenthesis:

$$
\begin{aligned}5÷(-2)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Applying PEMDAS to this expression, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}5÷(-2)^{2} & = \\ 5÷4 & = \\ \frac{5}{4} & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\overset{\frac{5}{4}}{\overset{⏞}{5÷(-2)^{2}}})\times (-\frac{4}{5}) & = \\ \frac{5}{4}\times (-\frac{4}{5}) & = \\ -\frac{5}{4}\times \frac{4}{5} & = \\ -\frac{5\times 4}{4\times 5} & = \\ -\frac{\cancel{5}\times \cancel{4}}{\cancel{4}\times \cancel{5}} & = \\ -1\end{aligned}
$$
